one_line: Claude's six fixes all landed and the pattern-as-memory fabrication is gone; residual flags are that the 'verifiable record' is anonymous in-text and the Goldman=group=application mapping leaves the multi-year contracts (printing/email) disconnected from the judgment-data thesis (video/travel).
new_introduced_issues: 'Every audit of this project has flagged the same thing: the founder is not a technical person' overgeneralizes what the audits actually flagged, but it functions as rhetorical framing rather than deception.
'One LLM grading another LLM's code' is slightly loose if the codebase is largely human/LLM-assisted work by the non-engineer founder; the parenthetical caveat partially covers this.
neither_caught: The Goldman-as-group vs Goldman-as-application seam: the cited multi-year stability evidence (textbook runs, email-server contracts) comes from verticals (printing, web) that produce none of the video/judgment data the thesis says the application's real output is; the judgment-data examples (tour, clip, client preference) belong to the just-launching sixth vertical, which has no multi-year contracts yet. 'The thesis is fed by everything the application teaches' bridges this by assertion, not argument.

The 'verifiable record' is asserted but not actually verifiable within the document: the ASX-listed education operator and the seven-plus email-server contracts are anonymous, with no links, leaving the same class of verification gap the earlier fabrication exploited — the residual doubt a hardened skeptic would still hold.
